subtitle: Gunboats carry the action across a changing sea

body: Blood Wake is Stormfront Studios' Xbox naval combat game, released in North America on 28 December 2001. Its fictional, Asian-influenced setting provides a campaign of raids, attacks, escorts and defensive missions fought entirely from small armed vessels. The player moves across the water while aiming the boat's weapons and responding to threats around the route. Sea and sky conditions help distinguish locations without taking the action onto land. The boat becomes both the means of travelling through the environment and the fighting platform that must survive long enough to complete the assignment.

Playable vessels range from small craft to more heavily armed boats, with primary guns supplemented by weapons such as torpedoes, rockets and mines. The available configuration changes how close a target should be approached and which direction is safest after an attack. Escort work also introduces something that needs to remain alive besides the player's own vessel. A successful run therefore involves movement as much as accurate firing. The player needs to maintain a useful angle, avoid surrounding fire and recognise when pressing an attack would leave the mission's more vulnerable objective exposed.

The campaign contains twenty-eight missions, while local multiplayer supports up to four players and unlocks additional options through story progress. Hidden boats and modes include a deliberately extravagant form of football played by armed vessels with a giant ball. Blood Wake received mixed reviews but sold enough to join the Xbox Platinum Hits range. Its unusual setting helped distinguish the console's early catalogue. Instead of treating the sea as an interval between land-based battles, it builds the entire action game around the speed, turning and weapon positions of the craft travelling across it.
